data.name: Flip the Table
data.detailed_description:
Do you sometimes feel like you just want to Flip the Table? Does your boss deserve some table flipping? Or is it just that you're out of coffee and want to throw a tantrum?
If you answered yes to any of the above questions, or even if you didn’t, this game is for you!

Flip the Table is a physics-based, ultimate stress relieving virtual reality game where your objective is to flip the table and break as much stuff as you can. After a long day or just for fun you can now destroy things without getting a huge bill!

Five different levels for all your daily needs: From your own kitchen to your boss’s office and beyond, there are five different locations where you can let out your emotions with different items and props.
Break stuff, get points: Double the satisfaction by getting points from breaking stuff! Better than real life, huh? Get rated from one to three stars and try to beat your high score.
Equipment to ease your craving for total annihilation: Baseball bats, ice buckets and even dynamite to help you smash, bash and wreck your way to victory!

reviews.review:
[h1]Played On: [b]HTC Vive[/b][/h1]

Flip the Table is another "break everything in sight" VR game, akin to free counterparts such as Smash Party and Break Time. Players are able to teleport around the environment, or walk provided a large enough play area is present, and either just haul off and start flipping tables or stack more items on them to gain bigger scores. It's a physics based game, so nearly every object can be interacted with and subsequently broken in some manner.

The catch here is that you have an unseen time limit, but each time you break another item you gain a little bit more time to continue wrecking stuff. There are five levels to play, with the ultimate goal of each one being to hit a score high enough to earn a three-star rating. The rating system feels like the three-star engine that nearly all puzzle-centric mobile games use, so it seems a little bit out of place on PC. Of course, even after the timer runs out you're free to keep on smashing things, but you'll more than likely have run out of items at that point anyway.

As the name would suggest, Flip the Table mostly revolves around putting your hands under some form of table and flipping it over. It's something that I'm sure nearly all of us have referenced in our lives, and I myself think about flipping my desk at work almost every single day. You would think this game would be a total fantasy come true, but it falls just a bit short of anything spectacular. This is primarily due to the fact that after you're finished flipping the table(s) in a level, the remaining objects just aren't any fun to destroy, most of these being books that are just filler content. Not to mention, the bat that's available in a couple of levels just acts like a foam or wiffle-ball bat and doesn't do much of anything at all.

With better haptic feedback integration, as well as a bit of in-game physics and item tweaking, Flip the Table could become very well worth its $2.29 price point. There's also a severe lack of music or a fitting soundtrack to break items by. After all is said and done, even attaining 3 stars on each level, about half an hour has passed. Does Flip the Table relieve stress and satisfy the urge to break things? Only just barely, and the free games of this genre do a better job of fulfilling that need. Smash Party has unique visuals, a great soundtrack, and the whole "smashing" stuff has a great tactile and arcade-like quality to it. Forego this purchase, and check out the two freebies mentioned instead.

[h1]Rating: [b]2.0/5.0[/b] - It's not awful, but it's not great.[/h1]
